name: Deployment Editor
description: A visual software packaging editor for creating Windows deployment packages using PSAppDeployToolkit (PSADT). Build automated PowerShell deployment scripts through a GUI with drag-and-drop sequences, project templates, and one-click script generation for SCCM, Intune, WinGet, or task sequences.
author: Tugay Taskin

securityCheck.aiSummary: The Deployment Editor's Intune upload workflow mostly follows legitimate admin tooling, but there are notable security concerns. Primary issues include risky dynamic code execution from PSADT files (potential remote code executionVector), temporary plaintext handling of credentials in memory during Graph authentication, and a policy bypass in MSI-related script. Also, placeholder secrets indicate misconfiguration risk. No obvious data exfiltration or obfuscation detected. Recommendations: remove or constrain dynamic Invoke-Expression usage, avoid converting credentials to plaintext in memory, avoid execution policy bypass patterns, and ensure all secrets are securely retrieved from a vault or managed identity rather than hardcoded placeholders.

noRemoteExecution.reason: Dynamic execution of code from Invoke-AppDeployToolkit.ps1: the script locates an 'adtSession' assignment via AST and then executes the Right.Extent.Text using Invoke-Expression. This enables executing content from the PSADT file at runtime, which could be manipulated to run arbitrary code.

noMaliciousPatterns.reason: Set-ExecutionPolicy ByPass -Scope CurrentUser; bypasses PowerShell execution policy for MSI information extraction. This pattern can weaken host security and is risky in enterprise environments.
